newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf workers shut two plants for 24 hrs.
newsitem.headline: Elf workers shut two plants for 24 hrs.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine temporarily shut two refineries on Thursday morning ahead of a scheduled 24-hour strike by some workers from 1200 GMT, a company spokesman said.
The strike by Elf Antar distribution workers at the company's Donges and Feyzin refineries was expected.
It is not related to a French truckers' strike which continued to disrupt deliveries by road from French oil refineries on Thursday.
The first one-day Elf Antar strike was at Elf's 95,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Grandpuits refinery near Paris on Wednesday. The plant is seen operational by the end of Thursday.
The Elf spokesman said the 211,000 bpd Donges refinery and the 120,000 bpd Feyzin plant would be working late on Friday.
Elf Antar unions say they are protesting about plans to cut 330 staff or 10 percent of the subsidiary's staff. A union statement said there was no economic reason for the job cuts.
It accused oil companies of worsening the social climate through aggressiove social and industrial policies.

Elf did not comment on the background to the strike but oil sources said any action which cut output amidst the truck blockades would likely have minimal impact. Refineries have been working out ways to restrain output if the truck strike lasts.
